articles.title: ‘Ten years of your leadership have been fantastic’: Smriti Mandhana’s heartfelt message for Harmanpreet Kaur
articles.summary: Smriti Mandhana paid tribute to Harmanpreet Kaur after being appointed the new captain of the Indian women’s cricket team, describing her former skipper’s
articles.body: Smriti Mandhana paid tribute to Harmanpreet Kaur after being appointed the new captain of the Indian women’s cricket team, describing her former skipper’s decade-long leadership as “fantastic”.Sharing a picture of Harmanpreet on her Instagram story, Mandhana wrote: “It's been a pleasure playing with you for so many years. Ten years of your leadership have been fantastic and together we will strive to bring many more laurels for our nation.”Mandhana was appointed as Harmanpreet’s successor on Tuesday after the 37-year-old decided to step down as India captain across formats.The 30-year-old Mandhana, who has been part of the Indian setup since 2013, has previously led the team in 18 T20Is and four ODIs. She will now take charge of the white-ball sides on a full-time basis.The left-handed opener has also enjoyed success as a captain in domestic and franchise cricket, most notably leading Royal Challengers Bengaluru to Women's Premier League titles in 2024 and 2026.Mandhana has been one of the leading figures in Indian women's cricket and has scored more than 10,000 runs across formats. Her elevation marks the beginning of a new leadership era for the team after Harmanpreet's tenure.Harmanpreet, who first led India in 2016, stepped down after captaining the team to a second consecutive Asian Games gold medal in Japan.Her decision followed a review meeting with the BCCI, bringing an end to a decade at the helm during which India won the 2025 ODI World Cup and retained the Asian Games gold.Mandhana's message underlined the continuity between the two eras, with the new captain acknowledging the contribution of her predecessor while looking ahead to the next chapter of Indian women's cricket.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: First time in top 10! Shreyas Iyer leaps 18 places in T20I rankings after maiden century
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer has made a stunning leap into the top 10 of the ICC T20I batting rankings after his breathtaking maiden century,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer has made a stunning leap into the top 10 of the ICC T20I batting rankings after his breathtaking maiden century, while Axar Patel has also broken into the elite list following a dramatic rise in the latest update.Iyer has jumped 18 places to seventh in the T20I batting rankings after smashing an unbeaten 102 off just 43 balls in India's series opener against the West Indies in Lucknow. The century, the first of his T20I career, has propelled the India skipper into the top 10 for the first time.The 31-year-old's explosive knock has also strengthened India's presence at the top end of the shortest-format batting rankings. India now have four players inside the top 10, with Ishan Kishan at No. 1, Abhishek Sharma at No. 2, Iyer at No. 7 and Tilak Varma at No. 10.Iyer's rise is among the biggest movements in the latest rankings and comes after an innings that underlined his ability to dominate an international attack from the outset.Axar Patel joins Shreyas Iyer in top 10Iyer is not the only Indian making a major move in the latest rankings. All-rounder Axar Patel has climbed 16 places to seventh among T20I bowlers, joining the top 10 after a strong week for India's spin department.There has also been a major change at the very top of the bowling rankings. Afghanistan's Rashid Khan has reclaimed the No. 1 spot, replacing Pakistan's Abrar Ahmed.Bangladesh's Nasum Ahmed has climbed three places to eighth, while teammate Mahedi Hasan has made an even bigger jump, moving up 10 spots to ninth. The changes mean there are three new entrants inside the top 10 in a busy update for T20I bowlers.West Indies batter Sherfane Rutherford, who struck a half-century in the series opener against India, has also been rewarded, moving 10 places to 37th in the batting rankings.Shubman Gill extends ODI reignThere were significant movements in the ODI rankings as well, with India's Shubman Gill extending his lead at the top of the batting chart.Gill's unbeaten 223 in the second ODI against the West Indies in Guwahati, which helped India clinch the series, has taken him to 841 rating points.West Indies captain Shai Hope has moved two places to sixth after his 162 in the series finale, while India's KL Rahul has surged seven places to joint 10th.West Indies left-hander Amir Jangoo has made one of the biggest jumps on the list, rising from outside the top 100 to 55th.Among ODI bowlers, West Indies pacer Jayden Seales has climbed 12 places to 10th, reaching a new career-high ranking after claiming four wickets in the series against India.USA veteran Milind Kumar has also reached a career-best position, moving four places to 10th among ODI all-rounders after his recent century against the UAE in the ongoing ICC Cricket World Cup League 2.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘This comeback is thoroughly deserved’: Suresh Raina welcomes Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s India return
articles.summary: Former India batter Suresh Raina has welcomed Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to the Indian T20I squad, calling the veteran pacer’s comeback a reward for his
articles.body: Former India batter Suresh Raina has welcomed Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to the Indian T20I squad, calling the veteran pacer’s comeback a reward for his discipline, hard work and resilience.Bhuvneshwar, 36, is back in the India setup nearly four years after his last international appearance. His India career had been on hold since the 2022 T20 World Cup semi-final against England in Adelaide.The seamer earned his recall after producing a string of consistent performances in the IPL, with Raina describing his return to the national side as thoroughly deserved.“Welcome back, Bhuvi! So happy to see one of India’s finest and most skilful bowlers getting his recognition again. The discipline, hard work and resilience he has shown over the years is truly inspiring. From Uttar Pradesh to the IPL, and now back in the Indian T20 side, this comeback is thoroughly deserved. Keep inspiring, @BhuviOfficial. Your journey is a reminder that hard work always finds its way back,” Raina wrote in an X post.Bhuvneshwar has represented India in 229 matches across formats, taking 294 wickets at an average of 29.50. His tally includes seven five-wicket hauls.His return comes ahead of India’s tour, which begins with a five-match T20I series from October 22. The T20I leg will be followed by five ODIs and two Tests.Raina highlighted Bhuvneshwar’s journey from Uttar Pradesh through the IPL and back into the Indian team as an example of perseverance paying off.The veteran pacer will now have another opportunity to add to his India career after almost four years away from the international setup.India’s T20I Squad: Shreyas Iyer [C], Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson [WK], Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan [WK], Tilak Varma [VC], Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Hundred has silenced all of them’: Sunil Gavaskar hails Shreyas Iyer after sublime maiden T20I ton
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Shreyas Iyer's maiden T20I century came at a crucial juncture in his captaincy, and the sublime knock has silenced questions over his batting
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shreyas Iyer's maiden T20I century came at a crucial juncture in his captaincy, and the sublime knock has silenced questions over his batting form, according to India great Sunil Gavaskar.Iyer had crossed the 50-run mark only twice since taking over as India's T20I captain in June, but he produced a stunning response in the opening match of the five-game series against the West Indies in Lucknow on Tuesday.The right-hander smashed an unbeaten 102 off just 43 balls, including a rapid acceleration after reaching his fifty in 28 deliveries, to guide India to a dominant eight-wicket victory and a 1-0 series lead.“It was a sublime knock from Shreyas Iyer. He looked unstoppable, and no matter what lines and lengths the West Indian bowlers bowled, Iyer had an answer to everything,” Gavaskar said on JioStar.ALSO READ: First time in top 10! Shreyas Iyer leaps 18 places in T20I rankings after maiden century‘This hundred has silenced all of them’Gavaskar said the century was particularly significant given Iyer's recent struggles with the bat since taking over the captaincy.“Shreyas Iyer has had a bit of a torrid time with the bat since becoming the captain of this Indian T20I squad. In recent times, the wins have come, but his own form with the bat was a concern,” he said. “So, it was important for him to play a big knock, and he delivered in this first T20I.”Iyer took complete control of India's chase, reaching his half-century in 28 balls before shifting gears dramatically. He scored the next 52 runs from just 15 deliveries to complete his maiden T20I hundred in spectacular fashion.“There had been questions on social media about Shreyas' batting form, and this hundred has silenced all of them. This knock is a strong signal that Shreyas Iyer is back to his best,” Gavaskar said.The knock also came after India returned from Japan following their Asian Games gold-medal triumph. Iyer admitted the exhausting travel had left him fatigued but refused to use jet lag as an excuse.“After the exhausting travel, didn't realise where I was. Everyday I need to wake up like this! Bowling first helped us a lot. We just didn't look at jetlag as an excuse,” Iyer said. “Exultant! Was thinking about my first century and dreams do come true.”India chased down West Indies' 171 in just 14.4 overs, with Iyer's unbeaten century providing the foundation for the emphatic win.“Winning tastes different. If it is your day, win the match for the team. Overall it was a comprehensive performance. If we continue with the same mindset we will be one of the most destructive teams in T20,” Iyer said.For West Indies, captain Shai Hope rued a chaotic batting display and a lack of runs towards the end of their innings. Hope and Sherfane Rutherford had put on 63 off 35 balls but West Indies lost four quick wickets and were bowled out for 171.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India tour of New Zealand: Why ODI squad announcement was delayed
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The squads for the five-match ODI series between India and New Zealand and the subsequent Tests are likely to be announced next week.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The squads for the five-match ODI series between India and New Zealand and the subsequent Tests are likely to be announced next week. The ODI series opener between India and New Zealand will take place on November 4 in Auckland. TimesofIndia.com has learnt that the selectors want to evaluate a few players in the ongoing unofficial ODI series between India A and Australia A. Selectors plan to keep an alternate squad ready for the last two ODIs as the Test regulars are likely to leave for preparations.The ongoing India A series has given key decision-makers an opportunity to see how the ODI hopefuls fare against a quality opposition. A few players from this group are set to make the ODI squad for the last two fixtures.After dominating the four-day matches, India A lost their first 50-over game by 125 runs. The likes of Sai Sudharsan, Devdutt Padikkal, Prabhsimran Singh and Suryansh Shedge were blown away by the 21-year-old tearaway quick Mahli Beardman. The Western Australia speedster, who was out of action for seven months after being diagnosed with a lumbar bone stress fracture, returned with bowling figures of 4 for 23.Only Rajat Patidar (53) showed some fight against the Australian quicks as India A were folded for 149 runs while chasing 275.India on Tuesday named their T20I squad for the upcoming tour of New Zealand, with captain Shreyas Iyer continuing to lead a largely unchanged group currently competing against the West Indies. The big addition is Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who returns to the T20I setup after last representing India in the format in November 2022.Selectors have also named the India A squad, which will play three multi-day matches against New Zealand A. articles.title: Sky Sports to show England's ODI tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka live from October 18-31
articles.summary: All seven matches live on Sky Sports, including final on October 31; England's first game is against Pakistan in Rawalpindi on October 20; Harry Brook's men then in action on October 22, 25 and 29;  Sky Sports will also broadcast England's Test tour of South Africa this winter
articles.body:
A deal agreed between Sky Sports and the Pakistan Cricket Board means all seven matches held across Lahore and Rawalpindi will be shown live on Sky Sports and NOW.

The sides play each other twice before the top two teams meet in the October 31 final.

England face Pakistan in Rawalpindi on October 20, while they then take on Sri Lanka at the same venue two days later.

Harry Brook's men return to action against Pakistan in Lahore on October 25 and will stay there to play Sri Lanka on October 29.

The series continues England's preparation for the 2027 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

Brook's side have won their previous two ODI series - 2-1 victories at home to India and Sri Lanka this summer.

All games live on Sky Sports and NOW, all times UK and Ireland

The agreement to show the tri-series further strengthens Sky Sports' position as the home of cricket.

Sky broadcasts all home England men's and women's international and domestic cricket, alongside England's tour of South Africa this winter and Ashes on home soil next summer.

articles.title: Sourav Ganguly asserts no conflict of interest as he takes Delhi Capitals coach job while heading CAB
articles.summary: Sourav Ganguly has said there is no conflict of interest in his taking charge as head coach of IPL franchise Delhi Capitals while continuing as president
articles.body: Sourav Ganguly has said there is no conflict of interest in his taking charge as head coach of IPL franchise Delhi Capitals while continuing as president of the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB), saying he has the order of the BCCI ombudsman.Ganguly will take charge of an IPL team as head coach for the first time after replacing Hemang Badani at Delhi Capitals ahead of the 2027 season.The former India captain has been associated with the Capitals since 2019 and has held several roles, including Director of Cricket for both the men's and women's teams. His appointment will be his first stint as an IPL head coach."Delhi will play well. I'm looking forward to it," Ganguly told reporters on Tuesday, as quoted by news agency PTI.Ganguly was speaking after watching India's 1-6 defeat against Uruguay in a FIFA international friendly at the Salt Lake Stadium.Asked about the potential conflict of interest arising from his dual roles, Ganguly said: "I've got the order of ombudsman."Ganguly also backed India's decision to play against top international teams, saying the exposure would help Indian footballers improve."It's a good initiative and they will learn in this way. It (the development) doesn't happen overnight. You only improve playing against good teams," he said.India had earlier drawn 1-1 against Panama in Bengaluru before losing to five-time world champions Brazil 0-4 and two-time world champions Uruguay 1-6 in back-to-back matches.Ganguly, who represented India in 113 tests and 311 one-day internationals, made his coaching debut last year at Pretoria Capitals in the South African SA20 league. articles.summary: The BCCI on Wednesday praised outgoing chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar, saying his tenure was marked by \"truly special moments for Indian cricket.\" \"A
articles.body: The BCCI on Wednesday praised outgoing chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar, saying his tenure was marked by "truly special moments for Indian cricket.""A tenure marked by some truly special moments for Indian cricket — three ICC trophies, two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games Gold medals, along with a run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final," BCCI said in a post on X."Thank you, Ajit Agarkar, for your commitment, conviction and contribution as Chairman of the Men’s Selection Committee. Wishing you the very best for the journey ahead," BCCI added.Agarkar's tenure ended on October 4. Former India spinner Pragyan Ojha is currently serving as the interim chairman of selectors, with Shiv Sundar Das, Ajay Ratra and RP Singh the other members of the men's selection committee.Earlier in the day, India head coach Gautam Gambhir also praised Agarkar, saying "history would be kinder" to him and that his belief in "team first" played an important role in India winning three ICC trophies during his tenure."Dear Ajit Bhai, an absolute honour to work with you. Those 3 ICC trophies are testimony of your conviction: Team first & Team ahead, always.. I must say, History will be kinder to you. Thank you for everything. My heartfelt wishes for your future endeavours!!" Gambhir posted.India won the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups and the 2025 Champions Trophy during Agarkar's tenure. He also oversaw a period of transition that included the T20 and Test retirements of batting greats Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma.Agarkar was perceived as a ruthless selector and remained non-committal on whether Kohli and Rohit would be part of India's plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sandpapergate: South Africa broadcaster on the 'fluke' which rumbled Australia
articles.summary: How a team of South Africa camera operators discovered Australia's sandpapergate scandal as it happened.
articles.body:
According to the man who helped catch them, it was blind luck.

Sandpapergate, the scandal that engulfed Australia eight years ago, was blatant cheating played out in real time on live television to a global audience.

As the Aussies prepare for their first Test series in South Africa since the ball-tampering controversy in Cape Town, the director of the TV coverage that day admits serendipity took down Steve Smith and co.

"The way the Australians were caught was an absolute fluke," Alvin Naicker, in charge of SuperSport's live broadcast from Newlands, tells BBC Sport.

Not just one fluke, but a series of them.

That the "leadership group" of the Australian team hatched their plan during the lunch break on that Saturday afternoon in March 2018; that an alert camera operator lingered on Cameron Bancroft when others would have turned their attention elsewhere; that the big-screen controller showed in the ground what was also being broadcast to millions around the world.

In understanding how Bancroft was rumbled, a little knowledge of how live cricket is shown on TV is helpful.

"Coverage of rugby and football is very coordinated. It's camera one and two, then when the ball is dead you tell the story with close-up shots," explains Naicker, a highly respected and popular figure in the TV industry with more than 30 years' experience.

"Because cricket has so much dead time, there is a lot more storytelling. There are between 80 and 100 people coming together and putting the story together in a matter of seconds, coordinated by the director."

Captain Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Bancroft later explained they cooked up the ball-tampering plot during lunch on the third day of the third Test.

Reverse-swing had been a key factor in the first two Tests of a bad-tempered series: Warner clashed with Quinton de Kock in the first Test in Durban, then Smith was involved in an altercation with Kagiso Rabada in the second.

Australia were exposed before the afternoon session was done, thanks to Naicker and his team. At the time, SuperSport were not on the lookout for cheating, despite the shenanigans of the first two Tests.

"No one mentioned anything to me," says Naicker. "The first Test in Durban spiralled out of control in terms of behaviour, then in Port Elizabeth for the second Test, there were still some fireworks going on. We still didn't understand."

Reports written live by ESPNCricinfo suggest the ball began reversing in the first hour after lunch, 35 overs into the South Africa second innings. In the 43rd over, Bancroft was caught in the act.

"The ball went to the wicketkeeper, then to Bancroft and he was shining the ball," says Naicker. "First it was on his pants, then the next ball, the cameraman happened to stay on Bancroft because he was not shining the ball on his pants, but he was rubbing the ball on his palm.

"When he threw the ball on, he put his hand in his pocket. The cameraman - and these are big, big lens cameras - he zoomed into his pocket. The slow-mo operator looked at it, spooled it back and forth, then zoomed in and could see the yellow spot."

Test cricket's biggest scandals - your results revealed

Bancroft's work on the ball was not shown live, but as a replay later in the over. Inside Newlands, the operator of the big screen – working independently from Naicker – showed the same footage.

"They take a feed from broadcast but they also have to insert their own graphics and commercialisation," says Naicker.

"Between deliveries they tend to stay with live play, then at the end of the over they go to their commercials or whatever in the stadium. It was quite fortunate that when we showed it, it was in between deliveries, not at the end of the over."

Bancroft would later admit he "panicked" when he saw himself on the big screen. Comically, he hid the sandpaper inside his trousers. SuperSport caught that, too.

"When Bancroft looked up at the screen and saw it, he removed it and put it in his jocks," says Naicker. "The cameraman recorded it. It still wasn't live, we played a replay."

Bancroft, with Smith by his side, was challenged by on-field umpires Richard Illingworth and Nigel Llong.

The opener turned out his pockets, revealing only a black bag for his sunglasses. The ball was not changed and Australia were not given a run penalty. Play continued, yet SuperSport were on to what had happened.

"Australia coach Darren Lehmann was on the walkie-talkie to 12th man Peter Handscomb, who went on to the field, then the umpires get involved," says Naicker.

"An entire team of cameramen played their part. There was one following the ball, one on Handscomb, one on Lehmann, one on Warner. They all told a story that I happened to put together with this great team of replay operators."

As for Naicker, there was no hesitation in airing what his team had captured, even with the realisation of the magnitude of what was unfolding.

"A lot of people who watch cricket on SuperSport will know we are quite brave in terms of being quite creative and editorially sound," he says.

"It was a natural instinct. It wasn't something I previewed with 10 other people to say 'What do you think, should we show it?' I just went for it."

The footage was pored over by Naicker's team of commentators, while his phone was "WhatsApping off the hook" with messages from around the world, asking him to show it again and again. Replays drew the attention of the third umpire, Englishman Ian Gould.

"He's got comms with me while I'm directing," says Naicker. "There was a moment when he asked me 'I think that's enough now, do you mind not showing it?'

"My response to him was 'I'm quite comfortable in what I'm doing in my job and I think you should do yours'."

When the day's play finally ended, Naicker and his team went to a bar and heard Bancroft and Smith confess in their news conference. Both men and Warner were sent home from the tour and handed lengthy bans. When he returned to Australia, Smith broke down in a tearful address to the press in Sydney.

"It became disheartening for us," says Naicker. "It started becoming emotional to see how they were feeling.

"The most difficult thing for me was to see Steve Smith shedding tears. That was not nice and never the intention. You have to have some emotion for those guys."

There was still a fourth and final Test to complete. Feelings were raw, and SuperSport's access to interviews from Australia was heavily restricted.

Naicker and his team faced allegations of bias, that they were somehow part of an orchestrated plot to take down the Australians. Now, with the Aussies back in town, Naicker maintains he would have pounced on the same "fluke" had it been South Africa caught cheating.

He also highlights the power of television. Bancroft and Australia were exposed mere moments after their act of cheating. TV viewers knew before the on-field match officials.

Naicker points to a conversation he had with Stuart Broad, who also faced tampering accusations for treading on the ball on a tour of South Africa in 2010 and is now building a post-playing career as a pundit.

"When you played the Broad footage in ultra-motion, it looked worse than it was," says Naicker. "He said he never realised how much control and power the TV crew has until he worked in the commentary box.

"I said that's what you have to remind your team-mates. You can't hide any more in international cricket. There are too many cameras and technology around."

articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Vishnu Vinod ready to leave his imprint as Kerala captain
articles.summary: KOCHI: Kerala's newly appointed captain, Vishnu Vinod, wants to leave his imprint on this team, but he is keen that his players feel free to express
articles.body: KOCHI: Kerala's newly appointed captain, Vishnu Vinod, wants to leave his imprint on this team, but he is keen that his players feel free to express themselves and play to their potential.The 32-year-old batter from Pathanamthitta, who also keeps wickets, takes charge of the Kerala team ahead of the Ranji Trophy opener against Jharkhand in Jamshedpur on October 11. "We are going into this season with a positive mindset, and all our energies are focused on the first game," he told TOI. "I want to leave my imprint on this team, but I also want the boys to express themselves and not worry about their spot in the squad."The core group is the same one that reached the Ranji final two seasons ago. The big change is in the dressing room, where former Goa batter Swapnil Asnodkar is the new coach. "I played several games against him when he was playing for Goa. He's like an elder brother," Vinod said. "We're working on getting players to perform to the best of their potential."Kerala pacer M D Nidheesh calls Vinod's elevation an aggressive move. "He's a captain who plays for results, very proactive and aggressive, with an out-of-the-box approach. He's very inventive with his field settings," Nidheesh said.He points to Kerala's last league game of the previous season, against Goa. "On a dead, lifeless pitch, Kerala still forced an outright result, ending a lacklustre campaign on a high, thanks mainly to Vinod's captaincy," Nidheesh noted.KCA secretary Vinod S Kumar says the game against Goa in Porvorim, in which Kerala won by 9 wickets, was what prompted the selectors to hedge their bets on Vinod."The team management and the selectors were impressed by how he marshalled his resources. It was a dead game for us, so we decided to give him a chance to lead, and he didn't disappoint."Kumar says Vinod endured a lean patch a couple of seasons ago, following which he bounced back via white-ball cricket. "He was out of form, but he got his verve back after strong performances in white-ball tournaments like the Syed Mushtaq Trophy."Kerala's squad blends youth and experience. The batting is led by Sachin Baby, Rohan S Kunnummal, Vinod, Mohammed Azharuddeen and Salman Nizar. MD Nidheesh, Eden Apple Tom and Basil N P spearhead the bowling, and veterans Jalaj Saxena and Aditya Sarwate are the guest players.They are placed in Elite Group C with Jharkhand, Odisha, Bengal, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Delhi, and Services.Squad: Vishnu Vinod (c, wk), Rohan S Kunnummal, Abhishek J Nair, Abhishek P Nair, Sachin Baby, Ahmed Imran, Mohammed Azharuddeen (wk), Salman Nizar, Varun Nayanar (wk), Jalaj Saxena, Vaishakh Chandran, Aditya Anand Sarwate, Anuraj J S, Abhijith Praveen V, M D Nidheesh, Eden Apple Tom, Pavan Raj, Basil N P.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Changed Shreyas Iyer’s grip, initial movement and backlift’: How Abhishek Nayar helped India T20I captain bounce back
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Since he scored an 80 not out against England in July, India's T20I captain Shreyas Iyer had been experiencing a rare slump in white-ball cricket,
articles.body: MUMBAI: Since he scored an 80 not out against England in July, India's T20I captain Shreyas Iyer had been experiencing a rare slump in white-ball cricket, where he’s usually highly consistent, having failed to cross 30 in his last 10 T20I innings.Soon after he landed back in Mumbai after leading India to the gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, where he was out for 13 & 21 in the semi-final and final, Shreyas, surely concerned by his dip in form, sought out his old Mumbai teammate, friend and 'mentor' Abhishek Nayar, India's former assistant coach and currently the head coach of Kolkata Knight Riders, for help.The result: Iyer cracked a brilliant 43-ball 102 not out, including six sixes and 10 fours, to fashion India's eight-wicket triumph in the opening T20I against West Indies in Lucknow.After his blazing knock, Iyer said in a video released by the BCCI on Tuesday that a conversation with Nayar had aided his performance. “I had a brief interaction with Abhishek Nayar in that period (during his time in Japan) where we were talking about cricket. I think that conversation with him helped me a lot in today’s performance. The key note which I observed in my batting today was setting myself before the delivery of the ball, and that worked perfectly. So, to create that momentum and rhythm was essential at the start of the innings, and it worked out pretty well.”TOI has learnt that Nayar went to meet Shreyas at his home in Worli in Mumbai, and the two, who go back a long way, had a long chat about what could be wrong with his batting. Nayar revealed that for a brief while, Iyer had begun doubting his ability to smash those trademark massive sixes that normally sail into the crowd.The productive two-hour chat session took place at Iyer's Worli home, during which Nayar ironed out a few technical things in Iyer's game. "I went to meet him and he was feeling that he wasn't getting the power to hit sixes. He wasn't feeling that he could hit a sixer. So, we spoke about some technical things and made some changes in batting. We spent two hours on his grip and backlift. I can't tell you what exactly, but I changed his grip and backlift a little bit. Basically, I made a slight alteration to his grip, the initial movement and his backlift," Nayar told TOI.While churning out one stroke after another, Iyer looked back to his confident self on Monday. "There was no issue with his confidence or batting. He was missing the 'feel' to hit sixes and that was it," Nayar asserted.It helped that over the years, Nayar has followed Iyer's batting closely. "I compared his old videos and tried to set him up to get to what is normally very comfortable with him. I did a little bit and set him up. It's such an old relationship. It's such an understanding, that it doesn't take that much time," the former India and Mumbai allrounder said.Since resuming his role as T20I captain this year, Iyer has scored 511 runs in 17 innings at an average of 39.30 and a strike rate above 149, including one century and two fifties.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘India’s archers have shown Asia what they are capable of’: Virendra Sachdeva after historic Nagoya campaign
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian archery returned from the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with its richest haul yet, winning nine medals — five gold, two silver and two
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian archery returned from the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with its richest haul yet, winning nine medals — five gold, two silver and two bronze — in a campaign that underlined the country’s emergence as a major force in the sport.The performance was marked not just by the dominance of India’s compound archers but also by historic breakthroughs in recurve, traditionally Korea’s stronghold. India swept all three compound team golds — men’s, women’s and mixed — for the second successive Asian Games, while the women’s compound team equalled the world record in the final.The mixed compound pair also secured India’s quota for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where compound archery is set to make its Olympic debut.But it was in recurve that India arguably made its biggest statement. The women’s team ended Korea’s seven-edition winning streak in the Asian Games to claim India’s first-ever gold in the event. The mixed recurve pair won India’s maiden medal in the discipline, while the men’s team followed up its previous success with a second consecutive silver.The campaign was capped by a historic individual recurve gold from a 17-year-old Indian archer, whose composure under pressure also earned India an Olympic berth.“Yet the defining story of these Games was written in recurve, a discipline long dominated by Korea,” Archery Association of India (AAI) secretary general Virendra Sachdeva said. “Our women’s recurve team ended Korea’s run of seven successive Asian Games titles to claim India’s first-ever gold in the event. Our mixed recurve pair won India’s first medal in that event, and our men’s recurve team earned a second consecutive silver.”Sachdeva said the performance was the culmination of years of investment rather than a one-off success.“These results weren’t a day’s success, but are the fruit of nearly fifteen years of sustained, collective effort: world-class infrastructure, quality equipment, international coaching expertise, sports science and regular global exposure,” he said.India’s archers also had to contend with difficult conditions in Nagoya, including long commutes, testing winds and heavy rain. Sachdeva said their ability to maintain their composure amid the challenges was a reflection of the team’s character.“Their poise through it all speaks volumes about their character,” he said.The rise of the women’s contingent was another defining feature of India’s campaign. From compound to recurve, the women delivered medals when it mattered most, adding another dimension to an already historic performance.“It is equally heartening that our women led from the front. From recurve to compound, they delivered whenever it mattered most, and they will inspire countless young girls across India to pick up a bow,” Sachdeva said.The secretary general also credited the coaches, support staff and families who have been part of the long-term development of Indian archery.“There were times when the podium felt within reach yet just beyond our grasp, but the faith of our coaches, support staff and families never wavered,” he said.Sachdeva described the Nagoya campaign as a landmark even by the standards of his experience in sports administration, recalling the attention the team received from the government during the Games.“Having been with the sports administration for a while now, I have witnessed many campaigns, but Nagoya was a first even for me,” he said. “While I was with the team, the Hon’ble Union Sports Minister personally called not once but twice to ask after our athletes, their preparation and their well-being.”For Sachdeva, however, the nine medals represent more than a successful Asian Games campaign. They are evidence of a new generation of Indian archers increasingly comfortable competing against the continent’s best.“When a nation honours its athletes, it begins to believe in them. Where there is belief, champions follow,” he said. “The medals of Aichi-Nagoya, won by young Indians who refused to be intimidated, are the clearest testament to this new sporting India.”With compound archery headed towards its Olympic debut and India having secured an individual Olympic berth through its teenage recurve champion, the Nagoya campaign has also provided a glimpse of what could lie ahead.“As for our archers, they have shown Asia what they are capable of. They are ready for the Olympics, and the world will soon take note,” Sachdeva said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Out on bail after rape allegation, Abhishek Porel named in Bengal squad for Ranji Trophy opener against Delhi
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Wicketkeeper-batter Abhishek Porel, who was recently granted bail in a case involving allegations of rape and other sexual offences, has been
articles.body: KOLKATA: Wicketkeeper-batter Abhishek Porel, who was recently granted bail in a case involving allegations of rape and other sexual offences, has been included in Bengal's 17-member squad for their Ranji Trophy season opener against Delhi in Kalyani.Porel, who has not played competitive cricket since the end of IPL 2026, was arrested in August following allegations that he had sexual relations with a woman on the promise of marriage. He was subsequently granted bail and has now been picked for Bengal's Elite Group C opener, with Abhimanyu Easwaran continuing as captain.The match will be played at the Bengal Cricket Academy Ground in Kalyani after Bengal's season opener was moved from the iconic Eden Gardens. The venue switch comes as Eden Gardens prepares to host Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the launch of the Durga Puja festivities around Mahalaya on October 10.Abhishek Porel returns to Bengal squadPorel's inclusion comes after he was also named in Bengal's squad for practice matches in Guwahati last month. At the time, a Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) official told Cricinfo: "His personal and legal matters are his own matters. If the situation changes, we will take the appropriate action. But for now there's no issue from our side."Porel was arrested by Mogra police in Hooghly district on August 11 following a complaint filed by a woman medical student from Karnataka. Police said the woman alleged that she had been in a relationship with Porel for around three-and-a-half years and that they had planned to get married.Police registered a case under several provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Section 69, along with provisions of the Information Technology Act. Hooghly (Rural) Superintendent of Police Kunwar Bhushan Singh had confirmed Porel's arrest at the time, saying, "There was a case lodged against him and a court order to arrest him. He was arrested late last night. He will be produced in court today."Shami, Akash Deep bolster Bengal pace attackPorel's inclusion apart, Bengal have named a strong pace attack for their campaign, with senior India pacer Mohammed Shami, Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep all part of the squad. Akash Deep, who is returning from injury, will be keen to get valuable match time as he looks to regain his rhythm and fitness ahead of India's New Zealand tour.Sudip Kumar Gharami has been named Easwaran's deputy, while Shahbaz Ahmed, who sustained an injury during the Duleep Trophy, has been left out.Bengal finished top of their group last season before their campaign ended in the semi-finals against eventual champions Jammu and Kashmir.Bengal and Delhi are grouped alongside Gujarat, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, Odisha and Services.Bengal Squad: Abhimanyu Easwaran (capt), Sudip Kumar Gharami (vice-capt), Sudip Chatterjee, Abishek Porel (wk), Shakir Habib Gandhi (wk), Ankur Paul, Sumanta Gupta, Ankit Shukla, Subham Chatterjee, Mohammed Shami, Akash Deep, Mukesh Kumar, Suraj Sindhu Jaiswal, Pradipta Pramanik, Aamir Gani, Md. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to international cricket could open the door for a remarkable
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to international cricket could open the door for a remarkable comeback to India’s ODI squad and potentially take the veteran pacer to next year’s 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.Bhuvneshwar, who returned to India colours after nearly four years when he was picked for the upcoming five-match T20I series in New Zealand, last played an ODI against South Africa at Paarl in 2022.Ashwin feels the selectors will be watching Bhuvneshwar closely in New Zealand and that a successful series could immediately put him in contention for the ODI side ahead of the World Cup.“He is going to New Zealand now. I am telling you, if he does well, everyone will immediately say, just take him for the ODI team as well. The selectors will be watching very closely,” Ashwin said on his YouTube channel.‘Nobody can stop’ Bumrah-Bhuvneshwar combinationAshwin went a step further, saying Bhuvneshwar’s ability to swing the ball and maintain decent pace could make him a valuable option in conditions in South Africa and Australia.“If he swings the ball and shows decent fitness, nobody can stop Jasprit Bumrah and Bhuvneshwar Kumar from sitting together on that flight to the World Cup, with Bhuvneshwar bowling the first ball of the World Cup,” said Ashwin.The 36-year-old seamer has played 121 ODIs and taken 141 wickets. His ability to move the ball both ways, particularly with the new ball, is a skill Ashwin believes could be particularly useful in conditions where seam and swing can play a major role.“Do you want swing? He has swing. If you want it to move one way, he can do that. If you want it to move both ways, he can do that too. And then he has decent pace,” he added.Bhuvneshwar’s recent performances in the IPL have also strengthened his case for an international comeback. He played a key role in Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s back-to-back IPL titles, taking 17 wickets in the 2025 season and 28 in 2026.Ashwin highlights one major concernWhile Ashwin remains bullish about Bhuvneshwar’s skill set, he stressed that fitness could be crucial if the pacer is to extend his international career and push for a place at the World Cup.“I am once again putting my neck on the line to say this: if he had worked a little harder, if the timing had been right and if he had avoided those injuries, with the skill set he possesses, he could have been a king for India across all formats,” he said.Apart from 21 Tests and 121 ODIs, Bhuvneshwar has played 87 T20Is and taken 90 wickets. His return also gives India another experienced seamer alongside the likes of Jasprit Bumrah, while potentially offering guidance to younger pacers such as Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav.India will play five T20Is against New Zealand later this month before the tour moves into the ODI and Test phases, giving Bhuvneshwar an immediate opportunity to make a case for a longer international comeback.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur: The captain who changed how India’s women played cricket
articles.summary: Kaur’s magical innings instilled belief in the Indian women’s cricket team before she led them to a first world title.
articles.body:
For nine years, Harmanpreet Kaur’s career as captain of the Indian women’s cricket team teetered on the brink of near-misses and lingering deliberations.

The biggest question centred on an elusive maiden World Cup title and India’s failure to cross the final hurdle at major tournaments.

Their breakout run at the one-day international (ODI) World Cup ended in heartbreak in 2017, a year after Kaur was appointed captain in the Twenty20 format and earmarked to take over the reins across all formats of the game.

Under her leadership, India qualified for but lost their first T20 World Cup final in 2020 and ended with a silver medal at the Commonwealth Games in 2022, before suffering another agonising T20 World Cup semifinal defeat in 2023.

In November 2025, the what-if was finally buried.

Kaur’s India beat then-defending champions Australia in a sensational come-from-behind World Cup semifinal before overcoming a resolute South Africa in the final to be crowned world champions for the first time – in front of adoring home fans.

Less than a year later, on October 6, 2026, Kaur stepped down as India’s all-format captain , ending a decade-long leadership journey that saw India transform into world champions after decades spent chasing cricket’s traditional heavyweights Australia and England.

“This is not an easy decision,” the 37-year-old wrote in an Instagram post, adding that she will continue to play international cricket. “As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions. Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost.”

The announcement was made after discussions on the future of Indian women’s cricket, which took place a day earlier between Kaur, Smriti Mandhana, head coach Amol Muzumdar and Devajit Saikia, honorary secretary of the Indian cricket board.

Mandhana, who was Kaur’s deputy for four years, replaced her as captain.

Kaur, India’s most capped women’s cricketer, enjoyed a leadership stint that included five Test matches, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, with win percentages of 80, 58.82 and 59.35 respectively.

The Punjab-born top-order batter’s last game in charge was the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan, where India stepped on the podium as gold medallists .

Nine days earlier, Kaur led them to an Asia Cup trophy in the United Arab Emirates.

The medals and trophies tell one part of Kaur’s tale as captain. The other lies in how India learned to play differently under her.

Kaur took over as India’s full-time T20I captain in 2016, after the team’s disappointing group-stage exit at a home T20 World Cup.

It followed a match-winning innings that helped India win their first T20I series against Australia in any format, and a few months later, she was signed as the first Indian cricketer in the Big Bash League, Australia’s franchise T20 cricket competition

It did not take long for Kaur, the batter, to announce her intentions.

Facing the mighty Australia in the semifinal of the ODI World Cup in 2017, Kaur played an unbeaten innings of 171 that took India into the final and challenged long-held assumptions about the power and aggression an Indian batter could bring to the women’s game.

Following the World Cup runners-up finish, which is widely regarded as a defining moment in Indian women’s cricket, the top-order batter recalled how her father’s friends would discourage her from playing big shots, saying, “Why do you need to attempt big hits when you know girls do not have power to clear the rope?”

“After watching [the 2017] World Cup, they started believing maybe my teammates and I can clear the rope,” she said in an interview with The Cricket Monthly magazine.

Years later, former Australia captain Alyssa Healy made a telling observation about her contemporary’s influence on the Indian team.

“What she has done in leading this Indian side, and [a] new generation of Indian women into the modern game, has been amazing to watch,” Healy said in 2023, before India’s Test match against Australia at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai.

At her first T20 World Cup as full-time captain in 2018, Harmanpreet led India to their first semifinal in eight years, while scoring India’s first T20I century with a 51-ball 103 against New Zealand.

It set in motion an evolution in Indian women’s T20s, a format they had historically struggled in.

India’s strengths had been better suited to ODIs, making Kaur’s task of shepherding a younger side towards a more aggressive, modern T20 game crucial and timely.

In 2020, India went a step further in the T20 World Cup, reaching their first final, driven largely by 16-year-old batting all-rounder Shafali Verma and legspin bowler Poonam Yadav. Still, Australia overpowered them in front of a record 86,000-plus home crowd at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground.

Despite her own poor performance in that tournament, Kaur evolved as a leader.

“Two or three years ago, I used to be a lot more aggressive on the field,” she said during the tournament.

“I used to lose my temper very quickly, but things have been changing within me. I have seen that change translate into results for me and the team.”

Then-India head coach WV Raman praised Kaur’s handling of a young side. “The most important thing as a captain is to make each member of the side realise that they are an integral part of that side,” Raman said. “In that regard, it was a challenge for her, but she has coped with it brilliantly.”

Kaur inherited a T20I side in transition, with an influx of younger players bringing greater fearlessness and athleticism.

After heavy defeats against Australia and England in a home tri-series in 2018, she called for “fit players who can run all across the ground”.

Her attacking philosophy extended beyond the physical aspect of the game and instilled a conviction that India could beat Australia and England.

Following the retirement of India’s iconic captain Mithali Raj in 2022, Kaur enjoyed all-format captaincy for the first time.

In the same year, India travelled to England and shocked them with a 3-0 ODI series win for the first time in 23 years. Kaur scored a series-leading 221 runs, including an unbeaten 143 from 111 balls.

The final match of the series was played at Lord’s Cricket Ground and offered a glimpse of Kaur’s leadership skills.

India’s all-rounder Deepti Sharma ran out England’s Charlie Dean at the non-striker’s end for the final wicket of the match. When the dismissal, legal according to the rules of cricket, threatened to overshadow the series sweep, Kaur publicly stood by her player.

“Well, I thought you would ask about the first 10 wickets because they were not easy to take,” she told the host broadcaster, matter-of-factly, when questioned about the incident after the match. “I will back my player because I don’t think she has done something which is not in the ICC rules.”

From chasing the best to becoming the best

Despite their growth, India failed to get over the line in big finals.

Australia denied them a Commonwealth Games gold in 2022 and knocked them out of the 2023 T20 World Cup in the semifinals.

Embarrassingly, India exited the 2024 and 2026 editions of the T20 World Cup at the group stage.

But under Kaur’s captaincy, expectations rose as India continued to win bilateral series against England, Australia and South Africa.

And in 2025, India won the ODI World Cup.

There was a neat symmetry to Australia being their semifinal opponents. Eight years after Kaur’s 171 knocked Australia out of the 2017 World Cup, her 89 and Jemimah Rodrigues’s Player of the Match innings of 127 not out helped eliminate the same opponents.

Verma, the all-rounder whom Kaur backed at the 2020 T20 World Cup as a 16-year-old, was named the best player in the final and credited her captain after Kaur announced her decision to quit the role.

“Since the day I made my debut, you’ve always been there for me, on and off the field,” Verma wrote on social media. “You’ve led us through some incredible moments and helped shape the team we are today.”

The final weeks of Kaur’s captaincy brought more silverware, but against the backdrop of dwindling returns.

The calls for 30-year-old Mandhana to take over as captain grew louder.

The left-handed opener has been India’s best batter in the past two and a half years and recently broke the record for most runs in women’s cricket.

And with the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy, slated for early 2027, and the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics in sight, Mandhana was handed the reins.

At the end of her four-year run as India’s all-format leader, the defining image of Kaur’s captaincy will be her role in ending South Africa’s innings in last year’s World Cup final.

From cover, Kaur backtracked to catch Nadine de Klerk’s lofted shot, prompting wild celebrations.

Almost a decade since she was first entrusted with a leadership role, Kaur’s final act was to end the country’s agonising wait for a World Cup.

articles.summary: Pakistan batter Hasan Nawaz said on Wednesday that he is still hurt by the team’s loss to India in the Asian Games gold medal match and believes “small
articles.body: Pakistan batter Hasan Nawaz said on Wednesday that he is still hurt by the team’s loss to India in the Asian Games gold medal match and believes “small mistakes” cost them the final in Japan.India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to win the men’s cricket gold medal at the Asian Games last week.“I am still disappointed and hurt at not being able to win the final. We made small mistakes and we paid the price for it,” Nawaz, who scored 96 in the title clash, told the media, as quoted by news agency PTI.Nawaz said facing India, the No. 1 side, was always going to be a challenge. He was pleased with his own performance but felt Pakistan let the match slip during the chase.“I am satisfied with my runs but losing the final was disappointing because I really believed we could win the game. I was playing according to calculation and knew they were one bowler short at the end with just one over from Bumrah remaining. But I think we made some mistakes in the run chase and lost,” he said.Nawaz also said he was happy to make a comeback after being sidelined for most of last year.“To make a comeback with a good innings against India was very satisfying individually for me.”He said Pakistani players have always tried to give their best when facing India.“I think the final is over now and cricket and matches will continue. We will also continue to make mistakes but I think to beat them we have to learn from our mistakes and become better.”Nawaz, who made his international debut with a T20I century against New Zealand in 2024, said he has been working on his game by playing plenty of grassroots cricket.“I think the bowlers and pitches you get in these matches help you become a better player in difficult conditions. articles.title: 'Naman Dhir has finished him': World Cup winner's big statement on star's T20I future
articles.summary: Naman Dhir made a strong statement on his T20I debut against the West Indies, and his performance has already led to questions about Washington Sundar’s
articles.body: Naman Dhir made a strong statement on his T20I debut against the West Indies, and his performance has already led to questions about Washington Sundar’s place in India’s white-ball teams.The 25-year-old, who has mainly been seen as a batting all-rounder in the IPL, surprised many with the ball in the first T20I. He bowled his full four-over spell and returned figures of 3/31 as India restricted the West Indies to 171.Dhir had scored 318 runs in IPL 2026 but did not bowl a single over during the tournament. His international debut showed that he can offer India another option with the ball.Former India cricketer and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth believes Dhir’s emergence could seriously hurt Washington Sundar’s chances in white-ball cricket.Srikkanth: 'Naman Dhir has finished him'Srikkanth pointed out that Dhir initially came into the team as a replacement but has now made it difficult for the selectors to leave him out."Naman Dhir has now come in at Washington Sundar's place as a replacement player. Washington Sundar keeps getting injured after every two matches. Now Naman Dhir has come in as his replacement and finished him. How can you drop Naman Dhir now from ODIs and T20Is? He has immediately grabbed that spot. Now Washington Sundar can only play for India in Test cricket," Srikkanth said on his YouTube channel.Srikkanth was also impressed by how Dhir adjusted his bowling after getting hit."When he bowls fast, he gets hit for sixes. So he immediately slows the ball down, which shows that he's a very thoughtful bowler. He's ideal for T20 cricket. He bowls in such a way that he envisions himself batting and how one would bowl to him. That's how much of a thinking cricketer he looks to be. That's why he's an intelligent bowler."Why Srikkanth wants Impact Player rule removedDhir’s performance also made Srikkanth question the impact of the IPL’s Impact Player rule."This is why the Impact Player rule should be removed in the IPL. That's how you'll produce genuine all-rounders. Now you've got a good batting all-rounder in Naman Dhir. Today he bowled four overs, but even if he gives you two overs on a consistent basis, it'll be huge for India and MI," said Srikkanth.Srikkanth expects Dhir to get more opportunities with the ball in the IPL as well."He'll take loads of wickets even in the upcoming IPL. He must have bowled only 10 overs maximum in his IPL career, yet he bowled four overs today. He has everything, including luck."Dhir says bowling has always been part of his gameDhir, however, made it clear that his bowling was not something he suddenly picked up for his international debut.“I have been bowling for quite some time; it is not as if I have just started now. In the IPL, because of the impact-player rule, you don’t see me bowling as much. But it is not that I haven’t bowled. I have bowled a lot and have good experience here as well. Hopefully, I will continue doing well in the future,” Dhir said in the post-match press conference after helping India bowl out West Indies for 171 in the first T20I here.He explained that he followed a simple plan after watching Axar Patel bowl earlier in the innings.“I saw Axar Bhai bowling earlier, and he was bowling a little slower and getting some turn. That was in my mind - if I bowled a little slower, there would be good grip from the wicket, and I could get them out. So I just stuck to my plans and kept things basic. I think I got a good result from that," Dhir said.'I am working just as hard on my bowling'Dhir also stressed that his bowling has always received the same attention as his batting.“Again, I will say that even if you haven’t seen me bowling, I have been bowling as much as I have since I came here and I have practised just as much before this. It is not as if, as a batting all-rounder or bowling all-rounder, I have neglected one aspect. Yes, my batting is a plus point, but at the same time I am working just as hard on my bowling,” he said.“Whether I have to bowl four overs, two overs or even one-day cricket, where I have bowled six or seven overs, it is normal for me. I just have to focus on my plans and try to execute them,” he added.India, who won the three-match ODI series 2-1, are leading the five-match T20I series 1-0.The second T20I match will be playd on Friday at the JSCA International Stadium Complex in Ranchi.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Unko select karke koi meherbani nahi ki': Wasim Jaffer on Bhuvneshwar Kumar's India return
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to India’s T20I squad has received strong backing from former India batter Wasim Jaffer, who believes the experienced pacer’s
articles.body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to India’s T20I squad has received strong backing from former India batter Wasim Jaffer, who believes the experienced pacer’s selection is based on his performances and fitness, rather than any favour.Bhuvneshwar, 36, has been recalled for India’s five-match T20I series against New Zealand, beginning October 22. Jaffer feels the veteran seamer should have been brought back into the national setup earlier.“Der aye durust aye. Wo deserve karte hain (Better late than never. He deserves this). Unko select karke koi meherbani nahi ki hai kisi ne (nobody has done a favour by selecting him). His performances have been there, and his fitness has been good. I am clueless as to why he was dropped earlier,” Wasim Jaffer said on his YouTube channel.India will play five T20Is from October 22 to November 1 in New Zealand. The first match of the series is at Christchurch on October 22, followed by second on October 22 at the same venue. The third T20I, on October 27, will be played at Wellington while the fourth and fifth T20Is will be on October 30 and November 1 at Auckland and Hamilton respectively.‘Age ko thoda side mein rakhna chaiye’Jaffer pointed to Bhuvneshwar’s fitness and consistent performances in the IPL and for Uttar Pradesh while questioning why age was used as a factor against him.“He has maintained his fitness really well. Whenever he has the got oportunity, he has done really well. He has always done well in the IPL and for Uttar Pradesh. So, what was the reason he was not getting picked?," he said."Age ko thoda side mein rakhna chaiye (We should keep age aside). We have young players, but we should not neglect those who are doing well because you ultimately need experience when there is pressure. You cannot play with an entirely young team. You need to have that mixture of experience and youth,” Jaffer said.Bhuvneshwar has played 21 Tests, 121 ODIs and 87 T20Is for India, taking 90 wickets in the shortest format. His experience could also be useful to the younger pacers in the current setup.India's T20I squad vs New Zealand: Shreyas Iyer (C), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan (wk), Tilak Varma (vc), Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: SA20 Auction 2027: 18-year-old Jason Rowles becomes most expensive buy; Du Plessis, Pollard join JSK
articles.summary: The SA20 Season 5 auction saw established international stars and promising young players attract big bids, but it was an 18-year-old who emerged as the
articles.body: The SA20 Season 5 auction saw established international stars and promising young players attract big bids, but it was an 18-year-old who emerged as the biggest talking point in Johannesburg on Wednesday. South African Under-23 prospect Jason Rowles became the most expensive player bought at the auction after Joburg Super Kings (JSK) won a fierce bidding battle with MI Cape Town.JSK paid $174,248 USD for Rowles, making the teenager the standout signing of the auction.The St David’s Marist Inanda matriculant and rain Schools SA20 graduate is now set to share the dressing room with some of the biggest names in T20 cricket.‘The highlight of the day’Rowles’ price tag came after an intense contest between JSK and MI Cape Town, with both teams showing their interest in the young South African.SA20 League Commissioner Graeme Smith said the bidding battle showed how much the franchises value young talent."This year's auction showed exactly what SA20 has become,” SA20 League Commissioner, Graeme Smith said. “It’s become a home where world-class players like Faf du Plessis, Shimron Hetmyer and Trent Boult sit alongside South Africa's brightest young talent. Jason Rowles was the highlight of the day for me. Seeing an 18-year-old spark the biggest bidding battle of the day tells you how much the franchises believe in the next generation. It was only last year that he was participating in the Final of the rain Schools SA20 and today he will get to be a part of a squad consisting of some of the world’s best T20 stars. That's the pathway we set out to build, and it's hugely encouraging to see it working."Rowles’ signing also highlighted the SA20’s focus on developing South Africa’s next generation of cricketers.Du Plessis returns to Joburg Super KingsFormer South Africa captain Faf du Plessis was another major signing at the auction. The 42-year-old attracted strong interest from JSK and MI Cape Town before JSK secured him for $162,286 USD.Du Plessis will return to the Wanderers, where he has played during the first four seasons of the SA20. He will also have experienced company at JSK, with West Indies T20 great Kieron Pollard joining him. Pollard was bought for $90,162 USD and will add power-hitting and experience to the Super Kings squad.MI Cape Town make big movesMI Cape Town also spent heavily, signing Proteas all-rounder Wiaan Mulder for $156,274 USD. They also brought in West Indies batter Shimron Hetmyer for $90,162 USD and added New Zealand fast bowler Trent Boult, along with 21-year-old Oliver Whitehead.Pretoria Capitals strengthened their batting with former Proteas batter Rassie van der Dussen, who was bought for $30,053 USD.The Capitals also added Proteas Test and ODI captain Temba Bavuma, who will return to the SA20 for his third stint after being part of the Sunrisers Eastern Cape teams that won their first two titles.Sunrisers complete their squadThree-time champions Sunrisers Eastern Cape completed their 19-player squad with Proteas left-arm seamer Nandre Burger and England all-rounder Craig Overton.Burger will join a strong pace attack that already features Anrich Nortje, Marco Jansen, Adam Milne and Lutho Sipamla.JSK also added USA batter Andries Gous and Zimbabwe fast bowler Blessing Muzarabani as the league continued to attract players from different parts of the world.Smith was pleased to see several South African players find teams at the auction."It's also really pleasing to see so many Proteas players being picked up today,” Smith added. "A strong League and a strong national team go hand in hand, and today was a good example of that.”SA20 Season 5 starts in JanuaryThe fifth season of the SA20 will begin on Sunday, January 17, 2027.Sunrisers Eastern Cape will host Pretoria Capitals at St George’s Park in Gqeberha in a repeat of last season’s final.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Bengaluru: With the game of cricket constantly evolving, the International Cricket Council (ICC) made a slew of changes to its playing conditions, which
articles.body: Bengaluru: With the game of cricket constantly evolving, the International Cricket Council (ICC) made a slew of changes to its playing conditions, which came into effect from Oct 1. Some of those changes included a pink-ball trial in Tests and time-wasting penalties.Fraser Stewart, the Head of Cricket at Marylebone Cricket Club, opened up beyond the laws in a media interaction here on Monday.Modern cricket is batter-friendly, and now the ICC playing conditions say five penalty runs for time-wasting. Is it a way of levelling the playing field?The law has always been there. It’s just rarely been enacted, and I think now the ICC have said, right, we’re going to try to toughen up on this a bit. I think the more we can do to try to speed up play, the better it is. Otherwise, the public who pay a lot of money to watch cricket feel short-changed.I think what the umpires try to do is to highlight to players that there are laws that cover this and if you waste time, it will catch up and there will be an in-game penalty of runs rather than a fine afterwards.On pink-ball trial in day-time Tests...That’s an ICC playing condition rather than a law of cricket. I believe, in a bilateral series, say, India playing Australia, it’s for them to agree among themselves for a particular game, are we going to use a pink ball?Some people have thought you can start with a red ball and then when it gets a bit dark, you switch to pink. That’s not, as I understand it, what’s happening. Both need to agree and if they are happy to play with the pink ball, perhaps because they think that it’ll mean there can be more play after bad weather.One big concern is the over rates. How does MCC act on this?The laws do provide a remedy, both for batting and bowling sides. It’s for umpires to enforce those laws and, if they think the pace of play is too slow, whether it is the fielding captain or the batting side, and say, you’re on a warning; it will result in penalty runs.But the umpires do need to enforce that, and be backed up by the match referees.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Puducherry: Suryansh Shedge was not even part of the original India ‘A’ squad for the unofficial ODIs against Australia ‘A’.
articles.body: Puducherry: Suryansh Shedge was not even part of the original India ‘A’ squad for the unofficial ODIs against Australia ‘A’. A late call-up, following Hardik Pandya’s withdrawal with a fresh shin injury, handed the 23-year-old Mumbai allrounder an opportunity. He responded in emphatic fashion on Tuesday, returning figures of 4-40, even though he failed with the bat as the hosts lost the match.Shedge’s journey into the national set-up has been shaped by opportunities arriving at the right moment. He made his international debut against Ireland in June after injuries ruled out Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy.Pandya, during his time at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence, gave Shedge some valuable advice.“He told me to master my stock ball, the target-area ball. That needs to become my USP because when someone is attacking you, you can always fall back on it. If that gets mentally set in your mind, you’ll find it easier,” Shedge said.“My stock ball is the hard length. The surprise could be a slower one or a quicker full ball. It’s about making the batter guess, because then the stock ball becomes effective.”His hard-length delivery proved to be his biggest weapon against Australia ‘A’. With the pitch slowing down, he quickly realised that bowling short of a good length would be more effective than pitching it fuller.“The wicket was a bit slower. After the first over, I realised that short-of-good-length ball would work here. articles.body: Lucknow: The Indian team management has started to invest in Naman Dhir for the role of a spin-bowling allrounder who can bat in the late middle order. Despite being an integral part of the Mumbai Indians batting line-up over the last three years, not many knew of Dhir’s bowling credentials. But he has managed to impress with his accurate off-spin during the ODI series and in the first T20I against West Indies here on Tuesday.Dhir stated that his steady bowling is not something that has happened overnight.“I’ve been bowling for a long time; it’s not something I’ve suddenly started doing. In the IPL, because of the Impact Player rule, you don’t always see much of my bowling. But that doesn’t mean I haven’t bowled — I’ve bowled plenty. This has been a really good experience. I picked up wickets here, and I hope I can keep doing well going forward,” Dhir said after taking 3/31 on Tuesday.In the high-scoring ODI series, which finished last week, Dhir conceded runs at only 6.3 runs per over.“I saw Axar (Patel) bhai bowling at a slower pace and it was turning. Then I thought if I bowl a bit slow, I will get grip from the wicket and get some wickets. So I stuck to my plans and I guess the result came out,” Dhir added.However, the 26-year-old from Faridkot said that he is still eager to get a good hit in the middle with the bat. articles.title: ‘You’re always looking for the next hero’: Kapil Dev on finding Virat Kohli’s successor
articles.summary: Greater Noida: Brand Kapil Dev was a thing much before brand was anything in Indian sports. His was a truly organic, everlasting phenomenon.
articles.body: Greater Noida: Brand Kapil Dev was a thing much before brand was anything in Indian sports. His was a truly organic, everlasting phenomenon. Today, it is being put to use in perhaps just the way it was always meant to be — playing it forward.As president of the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI), a role he has slipped into like the proverbial glove, the former India Test captain and 1983 World Cup winner is helping add huge value to Indian golf.On Wednesday, shadows lengthening at the Jaypee Greens Golf & Spa Resort course, Kapil sat on the clubhouse green, gazing benignly at the last of the groups putting home in a tournament named after him. Excerpts...How do you feel as an Indian sportsman to have a tournament named after you?They’ve done it without my knowing it. They contacted my office and it was decided. It should be a President Cup, not Kapil Dev Invitational. I am just a worker.Would it be right to say then, this is your third coming? First as a cricketer, then as a coach of the Indian team, now this...No, no. You can’t say coach. If I give you a job for 10 days, you can’t become a coach. I was not working even six months (as coach). I wouldn’t consider that a coaching assignment.How would you describe this role of yours?I feel very happy. If we can do something for golf. I love to do work for cricket but if they don’t invite me, I have to do something. So I feel very happy to do it for golf.Had you played golf when you were an active cricketer, would it have benefitted you...?Had I played golf then, it would have helped with concentration. One bad shot can get you out in cricket too, but here your target is small.A lot of active cricketers are serious golfers today...Just go and enjoy yourself. Cricketers should understand they are playing for pleasure and making the game more popular. If they want to be a professional then they have to have a different frame of mind.Define ‘different frame of mind’...You need eight to 10 hours (daily) workload. Golf is very, very tough.That brings us to this much-used point of workload management and injuries in cricket today. As somebody who’s never been injured playing cricket, why do you feel it’s so common today?I don’t think I can judge. Only those who are playing can.What does Hardik Pandya, for example, need to do to be available more often?Play more cricket.Do you think he’s not doing that?I don’t know. You play more, your body gets tuned to that. But if you play less and suddenly you play more, chances of injury increase. If your muscles are fine, your injuries are less.There’s a spread of cricket injuries over the last four-five years. Is there too much of the game happening?Sandeep Patil put it very nicely. ‘In our time we used to play Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, club cricket, other cricket too.’ In 365 days, if you can play 250 days, you’re in the game.Do you watch more golf or cricket today?I don’t watch cricket. Yes, if I see the highlights or something special happens, you definitely go and see and enjoy that.What do you think has changed in cricket?A little bit of equipment. The bats have changed. These young boys are very confident, much better. They get a lot more opportunities. In our time, if you’re out of the team, you have to play Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy. The opportunities these cricketers have is a lot.The board has given them more opportunities to come back and perform, like Bhuvi (Bhuvneshwar Kumar). He’s come back after four years because he played in the IPL, performed and bounced back. But here, more credit to Bhuvi than anybody else. Because in a cricketing sense, they really write you off very fast. But he kept on working with the opportunities that he got.In golf, more sponsorships are coming in but we haven’t had an international win in a long time...If you don’t give the golfers infrastructure, how will they improve? All top golfers, they still can’t walk in to play in any golf course. Give them a better place to practise and play. Then it’s a different thing altogether.Today, if you tell a top golfer to go play, they have to pay wherever they have to play, even at this course. As administrators, we feel very sorry for this limitation. The top 40 or 50 pros in this country should be able to walk in to play at any of the golf courses.Which cricketers do you love watching right now?Any young cricketer who we can feel has a future for the next 10 years, 15 years. Those type of cricketers. We have seen Rohit, Virat. We already saw Sachin. And they made us so proud. (But) you’re always looking for the next hero. You always ask, ‘Who is the next hero?’As a cricketer I like to see which is that young boy who has got that chance, who can replace Virat Kohli. And play for 15 years. That’s what my mind looks for.What about Vaibhav Sooryavanshi...?It’s too early. Does he have the ability? Yes. But there have been so many in cricket who came with so much ability, then faded out.Look at Vinod Kambli. What will we say about that? Vaibhav is 16 years old. Give him another three years, then we will talk. When his lifestyle changes, his thinking too will change. Then we’ll come to know how he will look after the next two years. That is more important than looking at his performance.For someone with a classical bowling action like yours, how do you look at someone unorthodox like Bumrah, who’s still the mainstay of the Indian team?He’s fabulous. Hats off to him. With that action, he’s proved people like us wrong. We never thought he could survive with that action and bowl so well and become world leading bowler. Tremendous.You spoke of Kambli. What more help does he need?Everybody can help him, only if he helps himself. I don’t believe in giving him money. I would rather pay his hospital expenses or rehab expenses. Why has he reached this situation? Kambli has himself to blame.Imran Khan is a good friend of yours. Are you planning to send a fresh letter for his release?As cricketers, we’ve done it twice already. That’s their government, their policy.
